newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican feeder head weekly exports, imports - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Mexican feeder head weekly exports, imports - USDA.

text.p: USDA said Friday that steer calves exported to the United States from Mexico sold four to five cents/lb higher than last week and yearlings sold firm.
Exports for the week were estimated at 7,000 head into Texas and New Mexico. Confirmed exports for the previous week totaled 5,338 head, against 5,489 head in the same week in 1996.
"Demand is very good for calves weighing under 500 lb. Trade active. Bulk of supply consisted of medium and large steers weighing 300-600 lb," USDA said.
Prices for feeder steers weighing 300-400 lb were 78-88 cents/lb, for 400-500 lb they were 68-78 cents/lb and 500-600 lb they were 66-68 cents/lb
Imports into Mexico were estimated to have totaled 4,000 head for the week with good demand, it added.
